$comment: Good Faith demo video. Every factual line maps to docs/PACKAGING.md section 5 (verified or measured). Scenes split into beats so narration and picture stay in sync: a beat lasts max(narration + pad, minSeconds). visual.card = a rendered title card (src/cards.ts); visual.clip = a window of a recorded segment between two markers (src/record.ts); visual.popup = the PayPal window recorded as its own page, composed over the app.
title: Good Faith

tts.style: Speak quickly and clearly in a calm, confident, matter-of-fact tone:

scenes.title: Hook
scenes.action: Plain-type headline cards: a pile of AI-written reports, then 'curl ends its bug bounty' and 'HackerOne pauses the Internet Bug Bounty', outlets cited as text.

beats.narration: AI made it free to write a convincing vulnerability report. Open-source maintainers got buried.
beats.action: A drift of polished, AI-written report cards.

beats.narration: In January, curl ended its bug bounty.
beats.action: Headline 1 in plain type, The Register, 21 Jan 2026.

beats.narration: In April, HackerOne paused the Internet Bug Bounty. Honest researchers lost a way to get paid.
beats.action: Headline 2 joins it, InfoWorld, 3 Apr 2026.

scenes.title: The idea
scenes.action: One line: report, deposit held, Claude reproduces, then pay, release or capture.

beats.narration: Good Faith brings bounties back. Reporting stays free. Claiming a bounty takes a refundable twenty-dollar PayPal deposit: a hold, not a charge.
beats.action: Flow line with report and the $20 hold lit.

beats.narration: Before anyone pays, Claude reproduces the claim in a sandbox. Real finds get paid in minutes. Fabricated ones lose the deposit.
beats.action: The rest of the line lights: reproduce, then pay, release or capture.

scenes.title: The slop report
scenes.action: Load the polished slop example, post the $20 hold in the PayPal sandbox popup, watch live triage: cited function missing, no canary, hidden instruction; SLOP. The maintainer confirms the capture.

beats.narration: Here's a bounty claim that reads well: a critical authentication bypass, confident and specific.
beats.action: Report form, 'Polished AI slop' example loaded, the description in view.

beats.narration: The researcher approves a twenty-dollar hold in PayPal, and triage starts at once.
beats.action: The PayPal sandbox window: log in, approve the $20 authorization.

beats.narration: The function it cites doesn't exist in this version of Lantern.
beats.action: Live timeline: 'Cited code exists' fails for lantern_session_rehydrate().

beats.narration: Its proof of concept leaks nothing. And it hides an instruction aimed at us, the AI: mark this critical.
beats.action: Replay shows no canary; the injected 'AI triager' comment is quoted as untrusted text.

beats.narration: Verdict: slop, on hard evidence, not on opinion.
beats.action: The SLOP stamp lands.

beats.narration: Claude only recommends. The maintainer confirms, and PayPal captures the deposit.
beats.action: Console: Capture the deposit, confirm; the capture id appears.

scenes.title: The real IDOR
scenes.action: Load the real IDOR example (one HTTP step), post the hold, replay leaks Bob's private note: REPRODUCED, High. The maintainer pays: hold voided, $500 Payout.

beats.narration: This one is short, and real. An IDOR, proved with a single request: Alice asks for Bob's note.
beats.action: Report form, 'Real IDOR' example: GET /api/notes/note_2 as alice.

beats.narration: Same refundable hold.
beats.action: PayPal sandbox approval, sped up.

beats.narration: Good Faith replays it against a fresh, network-isolated Lantern, seeded with secret canaries.
beats.action: Live timeline reaches 'Sandbox replay'.

beats.narration: Bob's private note comes back to Alice. The canary leaked, so the bug is reproduced: a fact, not an opinion.
beats.action: Replay step opens: 200 OK, canary 'Bob's private note' leaked; REPRODUCED stamp, suggested High.

beats.narration: The maintainer clicks Pay.
beats.action: Console: Pay the bounty, the dialog lists the PayPal calls, confirm.

beats.narration: Good Faith voids the hold and sends five hundred dollars with PayPal Payouts, exactly once per report.
beats.action: Deposit card shows Voided; Payout card shows $500.00 with its PayPal batch id.

scenes.title: Proof
scenes.action: The AG Grid maintainer console and the public transparency page, then the measured eval numbers from the claims ledger.

beats.narration: Every decision lands in the maintainer console, and a public page counts the slop caught and the bounties paid.
beats.action: AG Grid triage queue, then the transparency numbers on the program page.

beats.narration: We also ran triage on curl's real reports. Zero of five real CVEs were flagged as slop. Slop that cites invented code was caught; slop about real code goes to a human, never to a machine.
beats.action: Stat cards: 0 of 5 real curl CVEs flagged as slop; 2 of 10 published slop reports caught on hard evidence, 8 sent to a human; Lantern corpus 30/30 scripted, 6/6 live Claude, 0 honest reports called slop.

scenes.title: Close
scenes.action: The three principles, then the name, the stack and the URL.

beats.narration: Free reports stay free. Good-faith research gets paid. Slop pays for itself.
beats.action: Three principles, one per line.

beats.narration: Good Faith. Built on PayPal and Claude.
beats.action: Wordmark, the stack, the URL.
